/about.title: About — Michael Dock-Walshe
/about.description: Meet Michael Dock-Walshe and explore his interests in AI, software, systems, robotics and automation.
h2: Interested in how the pieces connect.
Where I want to go next.
h3: Learn it. Try it. Question it.
p: I’m Michael Dock-Walshe, an aspiring technology professional interested in turning technical ideas into working solutions.

My interests span artificial intelligence, software, IT infrastructure, robotics and automation. I want to understand both what a tool can do and what happens beneath the surface. I’m drawn to practical problems where research, experimentation and troubleshooting can make something more useful.

I approach learning by breaking a problem into smaller parts, trying an approach, and investigating when the result doesn’t match the intention. I use AI openly because it can make unfamiliar ideas easier to explore. That does not remove the need to read documentation, test assumptions or recognise what I don’t yet know.

AI-assisted development · Software applications · Systems and networking · Robotics and automation. Project-linked evidence will be added as work is documented; no proficiency levels are claimed here.

I want to keep building useful tools, develop a deeper understanding of connected systems, and contribute to practical technology work. This site will grow with the projects, experiments and lessons that support that progress.
Education, training and qualifications will appear here only after verified details are supplied.

/how-i-build.title: How I Build — Michael Dock-Walshe
/how-i-build.description: A six-step approach to building with AI, technical judgment and practical testing.
p: AI can accelerate the work. Understanding helps determine whether the work is any good.
Understand the actual need before choosing a tool. Establish the objective, constraints, users and desired outcome.
Compare relevant technologies, establish requirements, and identify likely risks before committing to an approach.
Use AI, code, existing software, documentation, automation or hardware according to the problem, not the trend.
Inspect the implementation. Question assumptions, check important details and identify weaknesses in generated output.
Check the intended behaviour, reproduce errors, investigate causes, correct faults and retest after changes.
Explain the system, record what remains uncertain, and define sensible improvements for the next iteration.

AI assistance is not one fixed thing. A project may use AI for explanation, planning, code generation, debugging or extensive implementation. Each case study should describe that contribution specifically, including what I reviewed, changed or rejected.
